content: As I happened to browse a few English wikipedia pages related to Lean and ITPs, I noticed that the articles are often simply very incomplete. A few examples:

• https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proof_assistant#System_comparison could use a snippet for Lean (I have one; adding it got lost in train wifi issues),
  • should one of the recent Lean projects (maybe LTE, diagonal Ramsey or Carleson) be added to https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proof_assistant#Notable_formalized_proofs?
  • https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lean_(proof_assistant) is not mentioning mathlib at all
  • should mathlib be a part of this category https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Category:Large-scale_mathematical_formalization_projects?
I presume even fixing the above could be a useful way of improving Lean's outreach. Is that a useful idea for the mathlib initiative, or a random hacking session?
We should read Wikipedia rules about COI before submitting edits. AFAIR, they don't like the idea of people writing about themselves.
